overview: Wessex was a kingdom in southern England. Under Alfred, royal support for reading and translation linked learned texts with the skilled production of books and precious objects.

items.text: Alfred commissioned translations of religious works from Latin into Old English. Copies circulated within his kingdom.
Some books were accompanied by reading pointers called aestels. The Alfred Jewel may have formed the head of one, but its function remains an interpretation.
The jewel combines gold, colored cloisonne enamel and rock crystal. A figure appears beneath the crystal, and an animal-like head forms the base.
An inscription names Alfred as the person who ordered the object made. The museum dates it to his reign, 871 to 899.
The figure beneath the crystal may personify sight, fitting a possible reading aid. The museum presents this identification as uncertain.
Alfred's law code drew on earlier West Saxon, Mercian and Kentish rules. His government also supported fortified market settlements, connecting defense with economic activity.
Wessex became the base from which Alfred's successors expanded royal power across England. This was a process of political consolidation, not the disappearance of West Saxon people.
